newsitem.title: GREECE: Tonnes of uncollected garbage choke Athens.
newsitem.headline: Tonnes of uncollected garbage choke Athens.

text.p: ATHENS, June 5 (reuter) - A four-day strike by Athens municipal workers has left some 5,000 tonnes of uncollected rubbish on the streets of the Greek capital, posing health risks due to high temperatures, officials said on Thursday.
Athenians and thousands of tourists were forced to dodge piles of rotting garbage piled up on pavements, outside cafes and even at the entrances of museums and archaeological sites.

"If the Athens municipality does not take the appropriate measures to declare the strike illegal in line with existing laws then we (the government) will do it," Deputy Interior Minister Lambros Papadimas told reporters.
The strike prompted health ministry officials to warn of risks to public health from mountains of refuse festering under temperatures as high as 30 degrees Celsius (86 Fahrenheit).
The municipal workers have blocked the entrance of Athens' main garbage trucks' garage to press demands that hundreds of their colleagues on temporary contracts be hired on a permanent basis.
